themes_detail.label: Lead contamination spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints surged to 4 cases this week compared to a 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% spike (z-score: 7.49)—signaling a potential emerging environmental health crisis in Fordham/University Heights that demands immediate investigation of affected buildings and water systems.
evidence: 4 lead complaints filed this week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (967% increase, z-score 7.49)
Lead exposure poses severe developmental and neurological risks to children—critical public health angle
District has 259 active building permits (142 alterations, 75 new buildings) that may involve disturbance of lead-painted surfaces
reporting_angles: Investigate which buildings/addresses triggered the spike and whether renovation work is disturbing lead paint or pipes
Interview affected residents and DOH to determine if this reflects a data collection artifact or genuine cluster of lead exposure incidents

themes_detail.label: Rodent infestation acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 14 cases this week versus a 6.4 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 120% spike (z-score: 4.08)—indicating a rapid deterioration in pest control across the district that threatens public health and housing quality.
evidence: 14 rodent complaints this week vs. 6.4 weekly average (120% increase, z-score 4.08)
Community Board has repeatedly requested more sanitation trucks and equipment—unmet need may be contributing to deteriorating conditions
Unsanitary condition complaints also elevated at 1,256 over 90 days, suggesting broader sanitation infrastructure failures
reporting_angles: Map this week's rodent complaints to identify geographic hotspots and determine if specific buildings or blocks lack adequate waste management
Interview DSNY about whether staffing or equipment shortages are hampering pest control response, and track the CB's long-standing request for more sanitation resources

themes_detail.label: Mysterious SPIT complaint surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints exploded to 3 cases this week from a 0.5 weekly baseline—a 500% spike sustained over 4 weeks (z-score: 5.66)—suggesting either a systemic building code violation pattern or a misclassification issue requiring clarification on what is actually being reported.
evidence: 3 SPIT complaints this week vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% increase, z-score 3.54; sustained 4-week trend with 800% spike, z-score 5.66)
SPIT is a specialized enforcement unit—elevated complaints suggest targeted or concentrated code violations warranting investigation
259 active building permits with 142 alterations could indicate renovation work triggering inspections
reporting_angles: Contact HPD to define what SPIT complaints capture and whether the spike reflects a real enforcement focus or data classification change
Cross-reference SPIT complaints with active DOB permits to determine if renovation projects are the common denominator

themes_detail.label: Homelessness services overwhelmed
themes_detail.summary: Homeless Person Assistance complaints rose to 5 cases last week from a 2.4 weekly average—a 110% spike (z-score: 3.06)—indicating strain on outreach and shelter capacity that may reflect a broader homelessness crisis in the district.
evidence: 5 homeless assistance complaints last week vs. 2.4 weekly average (110% increase, z-score 3.06)
Community Board has standing requests for senior center and public health programs—may indicate unmet social service demand
Spike timing (last week) suggests emerging condition rather than seasonal pattern
reporting_angles: Interview DSS, DHS, and local nonprofits to understand whether encampments are expanding, shelter capacity is maxed, or outreach resources are insufficient
Profile affected neighborhoods and street locations to identify hotspots where residents are reporting homelessness-related concerns

themes_detail.label: Elevator failures in multi-unit buildings
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints reached 38 cases two weeks ago from a 19.4 weekly baseline—a 96% spike (z-score: 2.84)—suggesting widespread mechanical failures in residential and commercial buildings that could strand elderly and disabled residents.
evidence: 38 elevator complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 19.4 weekly baseline (96% increase, z-score 2.84)
Spike is now 2 weeks old—receding from this week's most urgent signals but still above baseline
Elevator failures disproportionately impact elderly residents, people with disabilities, and families with young children
reporting_angles: Determine whether the spike reflects seasonal maintenance needs, aging infrastructure in older buildings, or a specific triggering event
Investigate response times from DOB and building owners to elevator complaints to assess enforcement effectiveness
